text:
alex.mueller: Heads-up — CloudTrail shows batch-worker@prod assumed-role listing objects in customer buckets it shouldn't. Likely tied to yesterday's RBAC refactor (PR #4123).

chandra.s: ack. Can you paste the event ids/time window? :eyes:

alex.mueller: window 2026-03-20T14:02:10Z — 14:07:32Z. sample event:
```
{ "eventTime": "2026-03-20T14:03:01Z", "eventName": "GetObject", "userIdentity": { "type": "AssumedRole", "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/batch-worker-role/batch-worker" }, "requestParameters": { "bucketName": "customer-xyz-prod" }
}
```

miko.k: omg. Did we change role bindings to include s3 read in the new role-mapping? I thought we scoped to internal-data only.

chandra.s: Looks like role policy attach happened via infra service-account sync. @infra-bot can you confirm which IaC PR applied the attachment?

infra-bot: Found Terraform apply 2026-03-20T03:15Z from PR #4167 by dave.h; resource aws_iam_policy_attachment.batch_worker_attach -> policy arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/S3ReadOnlyFromCustomerBuckets (managed).

dave.h: That was a centralization change; didn't intend to attach that managed policy to prod batch role. Investigating.

chandra.s: Emergency mitigation steps:
1) Revoke STS tokens for batch-worker-role.
2) Attach explicit deny statement to deny s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-*.
3) Revert PR #4167.

I'll run 1 & 2 now.

chandra.s: Running revoke:
```
# internal-tooling: revoke-session --role batch-worker-role --reason "emergency revoke"
# fallback: aws sts revoke-session-token ... (internal)
```

miko.k: For step 2, sample deny policy:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::customer-*/*",
      "Condition": { "Bool": { "aws:PrincipalIsAWSService": "false" } }
    }
  ]
}
```

dave.h: Reverting #4167 now. Will push revert in ~5m.

infra-bot: Revert PR #4167 merged (commit abc123) at 2026-03-20T14:12:10Z. Policy detach queued.

sec-rotations-bot: KMS keys used by customer-xyz: key/abcd-1234 — check key policy for AllowDecrypt to batch-worker-role. No explicit key grants found. Recommend rotating data plane keys if suspicious access occurred.

alex.mueller: Quick analysis: found 12 GetObject events, all smaller metadata files (<1KB), likely config reads. No PutObject. IPs from our EKS worker nodes. No evidence of exfil > 1MB.

chandra.s: Good. Still treat as P1 until we finish audit and notify compliance. @legal we may need to notify customers if data was sensitive (pending classification).

dave.h: Follow ups: add unit tests to infra sync to prevent managed policy attachments to prod roles; create deploy gate. I'm on it.

miko.k: Also add CloudTrail filter + alert for any S3 access by non-data-plane roles. I'll open an alert.

alex.mueller: I'll draft short incident note for customers and escalate to postmortem. :thumbsup: 

chandra.s: Thanks everyone. Closing emergency window once detach confirmed and tokens rotated. Will attach timeline to incident ticket #INC-2026-0319.
